rv.q: Metzler’s poignant portrayal of parenthood still resonates stronger than ever.
The show is at its strongest when it lets Jessie and Lina just exist as friends and new mothers.
This is a great comedy with dark edges, because it takes an honest look at being a parent, the power of female relationships, and the dilemma every working mother faces after having a child.

cn.t: Metzler's poignant exploration of new parenthood resonates with authentic portrayals of maternal isolation and connection. Strong lead performances anchor this intimate examination of how parenting affects women differently.
